question: What would a TV ad campaign for Punctual Pros look like?
html:
Punctual Pros TV Campaign

A Punctual Pros TV campaign would be zip-targeted connected TV (CTV) bought self-serve in the company's ~240 zips. It would sell the on-time promise the three brands already make, and it would be judged on booked jobs, not views (Punctual Pros ad plan, Oct 6, 2026).

Why CTV, not broadcast

  • Self-serve CTV now has $50-$500 minimums and roughly $15-40 CPMs with zip targeting (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • That lets a ~$22M franchisee buy TV only in its service zips. It avoids paying for the full Harrisburg or Philadelphia market.
  • Candidate vendors: Vibe, Disney Campaign Manager, Universal Ads and YouTube on TV screens. Vibe lists a $50 minimum per strategy and $15-35 CPMs (Punctual Pros ad plan).

The creative

  • Use existing claims rather than new ones: One Hour's "Always On Time... Or You Don't Pay A Dime!", Ben Franklin's $5-a-minute guarantee, and Mister Sparky's "America's On-Time Electrician."
  • TV's job is familiarity before the furnace fails. It should also lift branded search and Local Services Ads conversion.
  • Specs: :15 and :30 spots, 1920x1080, about -24 LKFS loudness (Punctual Pros ad plan).

Test design

WeekCTV element
1Tracking numbers, QR codes, site pixel; 15% of Tier-I zips held out
2"Storm Ready" :15 vs "We Watch the Clock" (cut to :15), split 50/50 by zip cluster
3Frequency check, capped at 3 per week
4Read booked jobs per 10k housing units, exposed vs holdout; shift 20% of budget to the winning cut
5Weather-trigger pacing in alternating counties
6Vendor split: Vibe vs Disney Campaign Manager or YouTube TV screens

Source: Punctual Pros ad plan.

Weekly test budgets are $8,000 in week 1 and $12,500 in weeks 2-5. These cover all channels. The excerpt does not break out the CTV share.

How it gets measured

  • Measure cost per booked job and geo-holdout lift.
  • Do not use completion rate. It runs ~94-99% by construction (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • The plan's $12 cost per site visit is an assumption borrowed from consumer-brand case studies. No home-services benchmark was found. Treat any CTV return figure as est. until the week-8 read replaces it.
  • The week-4 read is directional only.

Gaps in the data

  • The CTV dollar split and the expected booked jobs per zip are not in the excerpt.
  • A full channel budget, plus the ServiceTitan booking baseline by zip, would answer both.

Next actions

  1. Confirm holdout zips and tracking numbers in ServiceTitan before any spend goes live.
  2. Produce both :15 cuts to spec and clear the guarantee wording with the franchisor.
  3. Set the week-4 and week-8 read dates now and agree on cost per booked job as the decision metric.
  4. Request the CTV share of the test budget and a pre-launch booking baseline by zip.
